correctness.rationale: For c≥1, r≥2 and d_i≥1, the only simple cycles are the r forward-arm/return-path cycles, all with a common return path, giving strong connectivity. With q named colors the return is monochromatic with probability q⁻ᶜ and the conditional forward-interior events are independent with probabilities q⁻ᵈⁱ. This yields the stated polynomial for infinitely many q. Its highest degree is N; the product has a double or higher zero at 1, so P′(1)=c and D=N−c−1. Cyclotomic multiplicities count forward lengths divisible by each index and finite Möbius inversion recovers all length counts. Thus each permitted partition of D into at least two parts contributes a distinct polynomial, proving the census. For 0<x<1 odd r makes both terms in P/x negative. For even r write P/x=xᴰ(1−xᶜ)(H−1), with H=∏(x⁻ᵈⁱ−1)/(1−xᶜ). H runs from +∞ to 0 and its logarithmic derivative obeys xH′/H≤(−r+x)/(1−x)<0 by the geometric-sum bounds; hence the unique crossing is simple. For x>1 each factor in B=∏(1−x⁻ᵈⁱ) is positive, <1 and increasing. The invalid-color fraction x⁻ᶜ(1−B) is strictly decreasing there, and continuity and its value 1 at x=1 give strict normalized increase on the full stated interval.
residual_risks: Reconstruction is relative to the named family. The real-root count is only on (0,1); the normalized statement is only for these networks. Finite verification data are corroborative, not used for the universal proof.

evidence: Crew et al. Theorem 1 gives general contraction/include–exclude machinery; Theorem 3 gives density of real roots even for digon-free digraphs.

Their v1 Conjecture 2 asks monotonicity of P_D(x)/x^n on [n−1,∞) for every n-vertex digraph; it is not a theorem there. The 2022 article discusses dichromatic equivalence, but independent OA full-text retrieval failed.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The stronger general counting theorem covers the polynomial evaluation. Root density across digraphs does not bound the roots of an individual network by parity. An open universal monotonicity conjecture is not coverage of this theorem, and this proof works down to x=1 only within the specified family.

value.rationale: The family is natural: all elementary directed cycles share a return path, with arbitrary forward-arm count and lengths. A complete relative fingerprint (and hence an exact fixed-order census), a sharp parity criterion and a strict normalized interval form a full structural test family for the related general questions. The value is in these conclusions rather than the already covered inclusion–exclusion evaluation alone.
residual_risks: Does not settle unrestricted monotonicity, global dichromatic uniqueness, or the other real or complex zeros.
